html:
The Anglo-Portuguese Alliance is an alliance between England, now Britain, and Portugal, agreed in 1373 and confirmed by the Treaty of Windsor in 1386. It is the oldest alliance in the world still in force.

It began when both kingdoms faced Castile. English archers fought for Portugal at Aljubarrota in 1385, and King John I of Portugal married Philippa of Lancaster. Their sons included Henry the Navigator.

Over the centuries Portugal relied on British sea power against Spain and France, as in the Peninsular War. In return Britain gained trade privileges, as in port wine. In 1943 Portugal let the Allies use bases in the Azores. Each side has called on it again in modern times. See Portugal.
